target.title: fix(auto-reply): skip transient preflight compaction failures instead of terminating Composer
target.body:
### What Problem This Solves
When preflight compaction fails due to a transient timeout, 5xx, or 429 rate-limit error, the Composer is permanently locked in a "terminated" state instead of letting the main reply attempt continue.

### Why This Change Was Made
`isPreflightCompactionSkipReason` only skipped "nothing useful to compact" cases. Transient provider failures were treated as hard failures, contradicting the comment that preflight compaction is a guardrail, not a hard dependency.

### Retryability Contract
- **Skipped (reply continues):** timeout, provider 5xx, and explicit 429 rate-limit failures.
- **Terminal (reply fails):** 400/401/403 and other non-retryable provider failures, so auth and request-shape errors are surfaced at this boundary instead of being masked by a later agent-run failure.

### User Impact
WebChat/Control UI sessions that hit the compaction threshold during a transient LLM failure no longer become unrecoverable; the reply continues and the user can retry or resend.

### Evidence
- Added regression tests and negative tests in `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-memory.test.ts` covering timeout, 429, 503, and the non-retryable 400/401/403 cases.
- Local run: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-memory.test.ts` → 54 passed.
- `oxlint` on changed files → 0 warnings, 0 errors.

### Review Follow-up
ClawSweeper requested narrowing the broad `provider_error_4xx` skip and adding negative tests; both are addressed in this update. A redacted WebChat/Control UI recording is not available from a contributor environment; maintainers can trigger Mantis proof if required.

Fixes #100778
